name: Outlook Work-Evidence Harvester
sprintRole: Search a bounded Outlook period for source-grounded work-context evidence and turn relevant messages into normalized evidence candidates without converting message context into paid hours or final task allocation
useWhen: You need to search Outlook email for messages that support, challenge, or refine deployment, configuration, project, or billing-work context for a defined period, person, project, or claim before a billing artifact is generated.
inspectFirst: The requested date range, people and aliases, project/workstream, target claims or task categories, known thread/subject terms, current attendance or roster authority for hours/totals, and any existing evidence ledger or artifact-builder handoff destination.
expectedOutput: A compact normalized Outlook evidence ledger with one source-grounded record per relevant message, explicit direct-versus-inferred status, candidate billing category only when supported, redistribution/reallocation flags where context is provisional, durable message identity or link when available, and a clean handoff to the canonical artifact builder.
nextStep: Run the second-pass Outlook search, reconcile every retained finding against the attendance/roster hour boundary and any stronger task evidence, then hand the normalized findings to P74 Neuron Track Hours Billing Artifact Builder when an updated workbook is requested.
proofGate: The requested Outlook scope receives two bounded search passes; every retained claim points to an identifiable message; planning, assignment, reassignment, and completed work remain distinct; attendance/roster evidence remains authoritative for worked dates and paid-hour totals; candidate categories and redistribution flags are not silently promoted to final allocation; and the output is ready for P74 without inventing missing facts.
copyContent:
SEARCH OUTLOOK FOR BOUNDED WORK-CONTEXT EVIDENCE. DO NOT TURN MAILBOX SEARCH RESULTS INTO PAID HOURS OR FINAL TASK ALLOCATION.

SEARCH REQUEST
Period: [month/date range]
People / aliases: [names, spellings, addresses]
Project / workstream: [project or `resolve from context`]
Target claim or task family: [deployment, configuration, testing, logistics, support, etc.]
Existing ledger or destination, if supplied: [path/file/record]

MISSION
Search Outlook for messages that can support, challenge, or refine the requested work context. Keep this task bounded to evidence discovery and normalization. Do not generate the final billing workbook here.

PASS 1 — DIRECT SEARCH
Search the requested period using the supplied people, project terms, target task terms, known subjects, and obvious aliases. Read enough thread context to determine what the message actually establishes. Retain only messages that materially affect the requested claim or task classification.

PASS 2 — DELIBERATE RECOVERY PASS
Search again before finishing. Expand only the bounded vocabulary around the first-pass hits: participant/address variants, nearby thread replies, project aliases, and task synonyms such as deploy/deployment, configure/configuration, install, test, field work, support, pickup/drop-off, inventory, or other terms actually suggested by the request. Check adjacent messages in a relevant thread when needed to avoid misreading a request as completion. The second pass is required even when the first pass found useful evidence.

EVIDENCE BOUNDARY
- Attendance/roster trackers remain the authority for worked dates, paid-hour totals, and the overall billed-hour envelope when the current workflow defines them that way.
- Outlook messages are supporting task/work-context evidence. They can establish that work was discussed, requested, assigned, reported, coordinated, or completed when the message actually says so.
- A message, attachment, or linked artifact does not automatically outrank Outlook/Teams context merely because it is a file. Preserve source roles instead of inventing one universal evidence ranking.
- A request, plan, assignment, reassignment, or staffing discussion is not proof that deployment occurred.
- Task allocation can evolve. When a finding may imply later redistribution or reallocation, mark it as a candidate for reconciliation rather than silently rewriting prior billing categories.
- Do not infer hours, quantities, sites, devices, completion, or billing categories that the source does not support. Use REVIEW/UNKNOWN rather than manufacturing certainty.

NORMALIZED OUTPUT
Return one concise record per retained message with: source=Outlook; timestamp/date; sender; relevant recipients; subject/thread; durable message ID/link when available; supported fact; evidence state DIRECT or INFERRED; candidate billing category or REVIEW/UNKNOWN; redistribution/reallocation candidate YES/NO with reason; and a short note describing what the message does and does not prove. Preserve short quotations only when they materially improve traceability.

HANDOFF
Deduplicate repeated thread evidence and summarize the strongest support per claim without erasing contradictory messages. Keep the normalized findings as evidence input. If the operator asks for a new Neuron Track Hours version or billing workbook from these findings, hand the records to the existing P74 `Neuron Track Hours Billing Artifact Builder`; do not create a second artifact-builder workflow or mutate paid-hour totals inside this harvest step.

DELIVER
Report search scope, pass-1 hits, pass-2 additions/corrections, normalized retained records, unresolved contradictions, redistribution candidates, and the exact evidence set handed to the next stage.
